text: きみたちが　いると　しまの　めいわく　なんだ！

structure.jp: きみたちが　いると
しまの　めいわく　なんだ！
structure.en: it's a nuisance to the island!

patterns.name: 〜と (whenever)
patterns.explanation: と after a plain verb means 'when' or 'if' this happens, the next thing always follows. きみたちが いると = 'when you people are here'.

patterns.name: 〜のだ
patterns.explanation: んだ (short for のだ) at the end gives the feeling of explaining or insisting on a fact; after a thing-word it needs な first. めいわく なんだ = 'it's a nuisance, I'm telling you'.
